title: Silence after the sayings
summary: The people hear the sayings, then the land is silent for many hours as their astonishment stills their lamenting and howling for slain kindred.

explicit_facts.text: All the people of the land hear the sayings and witness of them.
Afterward there is silence in the land for many hours.
The people's astonishment causes them to cease lamenting and howling for their slain kindred; silence lasts many hours.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathered or broadly dispersed population is quiet; the text does not specify how the people are arranged.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's clothing, ages, individual identities, and precise location.

narration.text: there was silence in the land for the space of many hours;

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the hen-and-chickens comparison literally; it is part of the later teaching.

title: The voice speaks again
summary: A voice comes again to the people. It addresses those from the fallen cities and speaks of gathering and nourishing them as a hen gathers her chickens.

explicit_facts.text: A voice comes again to the people, and all hear and witness it.
The voice addresses people of fallen cities, descendants of Jacob and of the house of Israel, and says they have been gathered and nourished often.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people listen; the voice may be represented as off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: The source or visible form of the voice; no speaker appearance is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The hen and chickens are a figure of speech, not a literal visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal hen gathering people.

title: The invitation to return
summary: The voice continues, recalling that Israel would not be gathered, inviting the spared to repent and return, and warning that dwellings will become desolate if they do not.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says it often would have gathered the house of Israel, but they would not.
The voice says it will gather the spared house of Israel if they repent and return with full purpose of heart.
The voice says that otherwise their dwelling places will become desolate until fulfillment of the covenant to their fathers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people remain present, hearing the continuing voice.
unspecified_visual_details: The voice's identity and appearance; the audience's individual reactions in this moment.

spoken_dialogue.text: yea, how oft would I have gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens, and ye would not.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the voice

spoken_dialogue.text: if ye will repent and return unto me with full purpose of heart.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the voice

spoken_dialogue.text: the places of your dwellings shall become desolate
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The hen comparison and the warning about future desolation are teachings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a literal hen or a future destruction as happening now.

title: The people weep again
summary: After hearing the words, the people begin weeping and howling again for their lost kindred and friends.

explicit_facts.text: After hearing the words, the people begin to weep and howl again because of the loss of kindred and friends.

narration.text: they began to weep and howl again

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify particular deceased people or add individual biographies.

title: Morning after three days
summary: After three days, morning comes; darkness disperses, the earth stops trembling, rocks stop rending, groanings cease, and tumultuous noises pass away.

explicit_facts.text: Three days pass; it is morning and darkness disperses from the land.
The earth ceases trembling, rocks cease rending, dreadful groanings cease, and tumultuous noises pass away.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The landscape transitions from darkness to morning light.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise landscape, buildings, and appearance of the darkness.

narration.text: the darkness dispersed from off the face of the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not add specific disasters or visible damage beyond the stated cessation of these conditions.

title: Mourning turns to joy
summary: The earth cleaves together again and stands. The spared people's mourning ceases and turns to joy, praise, and thanksgiving to Jesus Christ, their Redeemer.
characters: the people who were spared alive

explicit_facts.text: The earth cleaves together again and stands.
The spared people's mourning, weeping, and wailing cease and turn to joy, praise, and thanksgiving to the Lord Jesus Christ, their Redeemer.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The spared people express a change from mourning to joy and thanksgiving.
unspecified_visual_details: How the earth's cleaving together looks; specific gestures or words of praise.

narration.text: their mourning was turned into joy

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text names Jesus Christ as Redeemer but does not depict him appearing in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jesus Christ physically present here.

title: The more righteous are spared
summary: The account states that prophetic scriptures were fulfilled and that the more righteous people were spared; it describes the destructions they escaped.

explicit_facts.text: The scriptures spoken by the prophets were fulfilled.
The more righteous part of the people was saved; they received the prophets and did not stone them, and had not shed the blood of the saints.
The spared were not sunk and buried, drowned, burned, crushed, carried away in a whirlwind, or overpowered by smoke and darkness.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of the spared people; the specific places of safety.

narration.text: it was the more righteous part of the people who were saved

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses report who was spared and what they escaped; they do not stage the separate destructions as present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the listed disasters or deaths happening in this moment.

title: An invitation to search the scriptures
summary: The narrator urges readers to search the scriptures concerning the destructions and prophecies, then says many testified of these things at Christ's coming and were slain for their testimony.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator calls on the reader to understand and search the scriptures about the deaths and destructions and prophetic fulfillment.
Many testified of these things at the coming of Christ and were slain because they testified.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of the historical witnesses; any location or manner of their deaths.

narration.text: many have testified of these things at the coming of Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The deaths are reported in narration; do not turn them into a present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show unidentified witnesses being killed.

title: Prophets testified of the remnant
summary: The narrator names Zenos, Zenock, and Jacob as testifying about the people and a remnant of Joseph's seed, and refers to the brass plates brought from Jerusalem by Lehi.

explicit_facts.text: Zenos testified and Zenock spoke concerning these things and the remnant of their seed.

Jacob testified concerning a remnant of Joseph's seed; the narrator identifies the people as a remnant of Joseph's seed and asks whether these things are written on the brass plates Lehi brought from Jerusalem.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Zenos, Zenock, Jacob, Lehi, and the brass plates; their presence in the narrated moment.

narration.text: our father Jacob also testified concerning a remnant of the seed of Joseph.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The named prophets and Lehi are mentioned in narration, not shown as present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the historical figures as physically present.

title: Narrative report of Christ’s manifestation
summary: The narrator reports great favors and blessings for the spared people of Nephi and those who had been called Lamanites, referring to the ending of the thirty-fourth year. He reports that Christ manifested himself to them soon after his ascension, showing his body and ministering to them, and defers the account of that ministry.
characters: the spared people of Nephi (reported only)
those who had been called Lamanites and were spared (reported only)

explicit_facts.text: The narrator refers to the ending of the thirty-fourth year and reports great favors and blessings for the spared people of Nephi and those who had been called Lamanites.
Christ manifested himself to them soon after his ascension into heaven, showing his body and ministering to them.
The narrator promises an account of Christ’s ministry hereafter and ends his sayings for the time being.

unspecified_visual_details: Any nonrepresentational background or typography used to present this narrative report.
The location, people's number and arrangement, Christ’s physical features and clothing, and specific ministering actions are unspecified.

narration.text: Showing his body unto them, and ministering unto them; and an account of his ministry shall be given hereafter. Therefore for this time I make an end of my sayings.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a narrative report and transition to a deferred account, not an enacted manifestation scene.
The reported showing of Christ’s body does not authorize staging this summarized event as happening now.
The ascension is mentioned only as an earlier event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not enact the reported manifestation or ministry, including as a flashback.
Do not depict the ascension or combine its timing with the manifestation.
Do not invent a visible narrator, setting, divine appearance, dialogue, teachings, healings, or reactions.
Do not depict blessings poured upon heads as a literal visible substance.
